name: How do I decide between extending central AC or using a mini-split for an addition?
description: Check your current HVAC capacity; if extending ductwork would overload your central system, a ductless mini-split offers efficient, zoned cooling.

mainEntity.name: How do I decide between extending central AC or using a mini-split for an addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: You will need to choose between extending your existing central HVAC system or installing an independent ductless mini-split system. If your current air conditioning unit has surplus capacity and your ductwork can reach the new space, tying into the existing system works well. However, if your existing AC unit is already sized strictly for your original square footage, adding rooms can strain the equipment. In many additions and in-law suites, installing a dedicated ductless mini-split provides independent temperature control without overloading your central heating and cooling unit.
